title: One WebGL renderer drawn into many 2D canvases
summary: One `WebGLRenderer` on a detached canvas renders each item into the top-left slice of its buffer (`setViewport(0, H − h, w, h)`) and `drawImage`s it into that item's own 2D canvas in the same task; an item re-renders only when dirty and within a `50%` root margin; one `2,000,000` px budget sets the pixel ratio for the set (`min(tier DPR, √(budget / Σ area))`); teardown disposes, then `forceContextLoss()`, and the 2D canvases keep their frame; hover / press turns one item, a tint under reduced motion, drawn once in the static tier
variants: Three.js renderer on a detached canvas, sliced viewport + drawImage (this)
raw WebGL2: one detached context, one program, per-item uniforms, then drawImage
one shared render target sized per item, read back with readPixels into ImageData (no drawImage of a GL canvas)
